items.lawCode: Amd §§26-408 & 26-511, NYC Ad Cd; amd §10, Emerg Ten Prot Act of 1974; amd §5, Emerg Hous Rent Cont L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4130

SPONSOR: KAVANAGH
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the administrative code of the city of
New York, the emergency tenant protection act of nineteen seventy-four
and the emergency housing rent control law, in relation to recovery of
certain housing accommodations by a landlord

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to expand rent regulated tenant protections
by limiting a landlord's ability to take possession of units for his or
her own personal use.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

This bill would limit a landlord's ability to take possession of rent
regulated units, for his or her own or an immediate family member's
personal use. The landlord would only be able reclaim units in cases of
immediate and compelling necessity and would permit the recovery of only
one such unit. Additionally, the bill would prohibit such a recovery if
a tenant is sixty-two years of age or older, has occupied the apartment
for fifteen or more years, or suffers from mental or physical impair-
ment.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Limiting a landlord's ability to recover units for personal use is an
important step towards protecting rent regulated tenants. By allowing a
landlord to recover only one unit when reclaiming units for personal
use, this bill would prevent situations where a landlord may force out
multiple rent regulated tenants for the purpose of converting the apart-
ments into a single luxury unit or in some cases, converting the entire
building into a personal house for the landlord. Additionally, some
landlords have attempted to use this provision to improperly deregulate
units by forcing out rent regulated tenants then inappropriately raising
rents while units are not occupied or occupied by relatives.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill in the Senate.

2018: A5771 - advanced to third reading.
2017: A5.771 - advanced to third reading.
2016: A3812 - advanced to third reading.
2015: A3812 - referred to Housing.
2014: A5177 - Passed Assembly.
2013: A5177 - referred to Rules.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately, provided that the amendments to
the rent stabilization and rent control laws shall not affect the expi-
ration of such laws.

summary: Relates to recovery of certain housing accommodations by a landlord; limits a landlord's ability to take possession of units for their own primary residence: permits recovery of only one unit, and restricts such ability if the tenant has occupied the apartment for fifteen or more years.
